q: The melting point and boiling point vary with ____.
e: The melting point and boiling point vary with pressure. Pressure is what this statement is using.

q: Two significant points on the pressure-temperature graph are the ____ and the critical point.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. Two significant points on the pressure-temperature graph are the triple point and the critical point.

q: At the triple point, liquid, solid and ____ phase may all exist together.
e: At the triple point, liquid, solid and vapour phase may all exist together. Vapour is what this statement is using.

q: At the critical point both the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same ____, and are therefore indistinguishable.
e: At the critical point both the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same density, and are therefore indistinguishable. Density is what this statement is using.

q: The melting point of ice ____ as the pressure increases.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The melting point of ice decreases as the pressure increases.

q: For an ice skater, the pressure of ice skates ____ the melting point of ice and melts the ice under them.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. For an ice skater, the pressure of ice skates lower the melting point of ice and melts the ice under them.

q: The boiling point of water also varies with the ____.
e: The boiling point of water also varies with the atmospheric pressure. Atmospheric pressure is what this statement is using.

q: An increase in external pressure will ____ the boiling point of water.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. An increase in external pressure will raise the boiling point of water.

q: The principle that an increase in external pressure raises the boiling point of water is used in ____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The principle that an increase in external pressure raises the boiling point of water is used in pressure cookers.

q: When a pressure cooker is in operation, the pressure inside it is ____ the normal atmospheric pressure.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². When a pressure cooker is in operation, the pressure inside it is twice the normal atmospheric pressure.

q: At twice the normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at a higher temperature of ____ and thus food can be cooked in a much shorter time.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². At twice the normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at a higher temperature of 120° C and thus food can be cooked in a much shorter time.

q: An object having ____ thermal capacity can be heated up easily.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. An object having lower thermal capacity can be heated up easily.

q: The temperature of mixture of water and ice will found to be ____.
e: The temperature of mixture of water and ice will found to be 0° C. 0° c is what this statement is using. 0° c is what this sentence is naming.

q: The ice is melting continuously until all the ice turns to water ____ its temperature.
e: The ice is melting continuously until all the ice turns to water without changing its temperature. Without changing is what this statement is using.
